_note: The DSX Scene ORBIT corpus (dsx-scene.md P5): controls="orbit" camera math as data. THE SPHERICAL LAW: offset = position − lookAt; distance = |offset|; pitch = asin(offset.y/distance)°; yaw = atan2(offset.x, offset.z)° (yaw 0 = camera on the +Z side); inverse position = lookAt + distance·(cosPitch·sinYaw, sinPitch, cosPitch·cosYaw). THE DRAG LAW: yaw −= dx·0.4°/px, pitch += dy·0.4°/px clamped to ±89°. THE ZOOM LAW: distance ×= e^(deltaY·0.0015), clamped to [max(near, 1e-3), far]. Each case folds `ops` (drags/zooms) over the state derived from the authored camera and pins the resulting state + camera position. Floats 6 decimals, tolerance 1.5e-6; numbers from an independent scratch implementation. Runners: TS (per-PR). Kotlin/Swift are the NAMED P5 follow-up.

cases.name: derive + round-trip — zero ops reproduce the authored position
a drag orbits — yaw −= dx·0.4, pitch += dy·0.4
pitch clamps at ±89° — no pole flip
an off-origin look-at — the sphere is centered on lookAt
